instagram_caption:
Before Parasite, Bong Joon Ho was a rich family's tutor. 🏠

In his early twenties, his girlfriend (now his wife) was teaching a wealthy Seoul family's son English. They wanted a math tutor too, so she put him forward as a trustworthy friend. He has said he was actually really bad at math. A friend vouches for you, and you're in: that's exactly how the con in Parasite begins. He says the job felt like peeping into strangers' private lives.

Fun fact: the Parks' glass mansion isn't a real house. Production designer Lee Ha-jun built it from scratch as a set on an outdoor lot, with the basement and bunker built separately. And the Kims' flooded street was a set built inside a giant water tank.

Parasite won the 2019 Palme d'Or, a first for a Korean film. At the Golden Globes Bong said: "Once you overcome the one-inch tall barrier of subtitles, you will be introduced to so many more amazing films." Then came four Oscars, including Best Picture, the first ever for a film not in English.

The twist: in August 2022, three years after the film, a real flood trapped a family in a semi-basement (banjiha) in Seoul's Sillim-dong. Three of them died. Seoul vowed to phase these homes out. Progress has been slow, and by recent estimates about 200,000 Seoul households still live half underground.
